Create a Transcript-to-Gene Mapping Table

Source: R/make_tx_to_gene.R
make_tx_to_gene.Rd

Builds a transcript-to-gene table from a GENCODE transcriptome FASTA file (parsing the |-separated headers) or from a GFF3/GTF annotation (through prepare_isoformic_annotation()). Parsing is done by DuckDB, so a full GENCODE FASTA (about 250,000 headers, gzip-compressed) takes a couple of seconds.

Usage

make_tx_to_gene(
  file_path,
  file_type = c("auto", "fasta", "gff", "gtf"),
  output_path = NULL
)

Arguments

file_path

Path to a FASTA (.fa, .fasta, optionally .gz), GFF3 or GTF file, or to an annotation directory.

file_type

"auto" (default) detects the format from the file extension; otherwise one of "fasta", "gff", "gtf".

output_path

Passed to prepare_isoformic_annotation() for GFF3/GTF inputs.

Value

A tibble with columns transcript_id, gene_id, havana_gene_id, havana_transcript_id, transcript_name, gene_name, tx_length and transcript_type. The Havana columns are NA for GFF3/GTF inputs.

Details

With an IsoformicExperiment object, use tx_to_gene() or tx_annot(), which read the same information from the annotation directory.

Examples

gff <- system.file("extdata", "example.gff3", package = "isoformic")
tx2gene <- make_tx_to_gene(gff, output_path = tempdir())
#> ℹ Parsing example.gff3 (GFF) into /tmp/RtmpmIi7db/example.
head(tx2gene)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   transcript_id     gene_id  havana_gene_id havana_transcript_id transcript_name
#>   <chr>             <chr>    <chr>          <chr>                <chr>          
#> 1 ENST00000282397.9 ENSG000… NA             NA                   FLT1-201       
#> 2 ENST00000615611.4 ENSG000… NA             NA                   FLT1-206       
#> 3 ENST00000617835.4 ENSG000… NA             NA                   FLT1-208       
#> 4 ENST00000543394.2 ENSG000… NA             NA                   FLT1-205       
#> 5 ENST00000540678.2 ENSG000… NA             NA                   FLT1-203       
#> 6 ENST00000541932.5 ENSG000… NA             NA                   FLT1-204       
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: gene_name <chr>, tx_length <int>, transcript_type <chr>
